title: 10. NLP, Transformers & LLMs: Word2Vec: Learning Word Embeddings
summary: Goal: Understand and implement Word2Vec - the foundation of modern word embeddings.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: **Goal**: Understand and implement Word2Vec - the foundation of modern word embeddings.

diagrams.title: Embeddings place similar meanings close together
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  ctx["Learn from context: words in similar contexts get similar vectors"] --> space["Vector space"]
  space --> sim["cosine(king, queen) high, cosine(king, banana) low"]
  space --> analog["king − man + woman ≈ queen"]
  space --> use["Use in search, clustering, features for classifiers, RAG retrieval"]
diagrams.explain: Word2Vec, GloVe and FastText learn dense vectors from co-occurrence, so related words end up near each other and some relationships become vector arithmetic. Sentence-embedding models extend the idea to whole texts, which is what semantic search and RAG retrieval use.

sections.title: The Problem with Classical Representations
sections.body:
### BoW/TF-IDF Issues
```
✗ High dimensionality (vocab size)
✗ Sparse vectors (99% zeros)
✗ No semantic similarity
✗ No word relationships
```

### Example
```python
Vocabulary: ["king", "queen", "man", "woman", "apple", ...] (50,000 words)

"king"  → [1, 0, 0, 0, 0, ...] (50,000 dimensions!)
"queen" → [0, 1, 0, 0, 0, ...]

Similarity("king", "queen") = 0  ← No semantic relationship!
Similarity("king", "apple") = 0  ← Same distance!
```

sections.title: Word Embeddings Solution
sections.body:
### Dense Low-Dimensional Vectors
```python
"king"  → [0.2, -0.5, 0.8, 0.1, ...]  (300 dimensions)
"queen" → [0.3, -0.4, 0.7, 0.0, ...]  (300 dimensions)
"apple" → [-0.1, 0.8, -0.2, 0.5, ...] (300 dimensions)

Similarity("king", "queen") = 0.85  ← High! Similar concepts
Similarity("king", "apple") = 0.12  ← Low! Different concepts
```

### Key Idea: **"You shall know a word by the company it keeps"**

Words appearing in similar contexts have similar meanings:
```
"The ___ sat on the throne"
  → king, queen, prince, monarch

"I ate a delicious ___"
  → apple, banana, pizza, cake
```

sections.title: Word2Vec: Two Architectures
sections.body:
### 1. CBOW (Continuous Bag of Words)
**Task**: Predict center word from context words

```
Input:  ["the", "cat", "on", "the"]  ← Context
Output: "sat"                        ← Target word

Visual:
  the    cat    [???]   on    the
   ↓      ↓       ↑      ↓     ↓
   └──────┴───────┴──────┴─────┘
        Predict: "sat"
```

### 2. Skip-gram
**Task**: Predict context words from center word

```
Input:  "sat"                        ← Target word
Output: ["the", "cat", "on", "the"]  ← Context

Visual:
  [???]  [???]   sat   [???]  [???]
    ↑      ↑     ↓      ↑     ↑
    └──────┴─────┴──────┴─────┘
   Predict: the, cat, on, the
```

### Which to Use?
```
CBOW:
✓ Faster to train
✓ Better for frequent words
✓ Smooths over contexts

Skip-gram:
✓ Better for rare words
✓ Better quality embeddings
✓ More commonly used
```

sections.title: Mathematical Intuition
sections.body:
### Skip-gram Objective

Given a sequence of words $w_1, w_2, ..., w_T$:

**Maximize**:
$$
\frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^{T} \sum_{-c \leq j \leq c, j \neq 0} \log P(w_{t+j} | w_t)
$$

Where $c$ = context window size

**Probability**:
$$
P(w_O | w_I) = \frac{\exp(v_{w_O}^T v_{w_I})}{\sum_{w=1}^{W} \exp(v_w^T v_{w_I})}
$$

- $v_w$ = embedding vector for word $w$
- $W$ = vocabulary size

**Training**: Adjust vectors to maximize probability of correct context words.

sections.title: Visual Architecture
sections.body:
### Skip-gram Neural Network

```
Input Layer          Hidden Layer       Output Layer
(One-hot)           (Embeddings)       (Softmax)

[0, 0, 1, 0, ...]  →  [0.2, -0.5, ...]  →  [P(the), P(cat), ...]
  "sat"               Learned             Context probabilities
  (50,000)            Embedding           (50,000)
                      (300)

Weight Matrix W      Weight Matrix W'
(50,000 × 300)       (300 × 50,000)
     ↑
  These are the embeddings!
```

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from gensim.models import Word2Vec
from gensim.models.word2vec import LineSentence
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.manifold import TSNE
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

# Set style
sns.set_style('whitegrid')
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (14, 8)
np.random.seed(42)
```

sections.title: Simple Example: Training from Scratch
sections.body:
```python
# Sample corpus
sentences = [
    ['the', 'cat', 'sat', 'on', 'the', 'mat'],
    ['the', 'dog', 'sat', 'on', 'the', 'log'],
    ['cats', 'and', 'dogs', 'are', 'animals'],
    ['the', 'king', 'sat', 'on', 'the', 'throne'],
    ['the', 'queen', 'sat', 'on', 'the', 'throne'],
    ['king', 'and', 'queen', 'are', 'royalty'],
    ['animals', 'need', 'food', 'and', 'water'],
    ['royalty', 'live', 'in', 'palaces'],
] * 100  # Replicate for better training

print(f"📊 Corpus: {len(sentences)} sentences")
print("Sample sentences:")
for sent in sentences[:3]:
    print(f"  {' '.join(sent)}")
```

```python
# Train Word2Vec model
model = Word2Vec(
    sentences=sentences,
    vector_size=50,      # Embedding dimension
    window=3,            # Context window size
    min_count=1,         # Minimum word frequency
    workers=4,           # Parallel threads
    sg=1,                # 1=Skip-gram, 0=CBOW
    epochs=50            # Training iterations
)

print("✅ Model trained!")
print(f"   Vocabulary size: {len(model.wv)}")
print(f"   Embedding dimension: {model.wv.vector_size}")
print()
print("Vocabulary:")
print(list(model.wv.index_to_key)[:20])
```

sections.title: Exploring Embeddings
sections.body:
```python
# Get embedding for a word
word = 'king'
embedding = model.wv[word]

print(f"🔤 Embedding for '{word}':")
print(f"   Shape: {embedding.shape}")
print(f"   First 10 dimensions: {embedding[:10]}")
print(f"   Min: {embedding.min():.3f}, Max: {embedding.max():.3f}")
```

sections.title: Word Similarity
sections.body:
```python
# Find similar words
word = 'king'
similar_words = model.wv.most_similar(word, topn=5)

print(f"🔍 Words most similar to '{word}':")
print()
for similar_word, similarity in similar_words:
    print(f"   {similar_word:12s}: {similarity:.4f}")
```

```python
# Compute similarity between two words
pairs = [
    ('king', 'queen'),
    ('king', 'royalty'),
    ('cat', 'dog'),
    ('cat', 'animals'),
    ('king', 'cat'),
    ('throne', 'palace'),
]

print("📊 Word Pair Similarities:")
print()
for word1, word2 in pairs:
    if word1 in model.wv and word2 in model.wv:
        similarity = model.wv.similarity(word1, word2)
        print(f"   {word1:10s} ↔ {word2:10s}: {similarity:.4f}")
```

sections.title: Word Analogies: The Famous Example
sections.body:
**"King - Man + Woman = Queen"**

Visual:
```
        Queen ────────────> King
          ↑                  ↑
          │                  │
        Woman ────────────> Man
           (same relationship)
```

```python
# Word analogy: king - man + woman = ?
try:
    result = model.wv.most_similar(
        positive=['king', 'woman'],
        negative=['man'],
        topn=3
    )
    
    print("🧮 Word Analogy: king - man + woman = ?")
    print()
    for word, score in result:
        print(f"   {word:12s}: {score:.4f}")
except KeyError as e:
    print(f"Word not in vocabulary: {e}")
    print("Note: Our small corpus may not have 'man'/'woman'")
```

sections.title: Visualizing Embeddings with PCA
sections.body:
```python
# Get embeddings for all words
words = list(model.wv.index_to_key)
embeddings = np.array([model.wv[word] for word in words])

# Reduce to 2D with PCA
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
embeddings_2d = pca.fit_transform(embeddings)

# Plot
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 10))
plt.scatter(embeddings_2d[:, 0], embeddings_2d[:, 1], alpha=0.6, s=100)

# Annotate words
for word, (x, y) in zip(words, embeddings_2d):
    plt.annotate(word, (x, y), fontsize=12, alpha=0.8)

plt.xlabel('First Principal Component')
plt.ylabel('Second Principal Component')
plt.title('Word Embeddings Visualized with PCA', fontsize=16)
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("\n💡 Observations:")
print("   • Similar words cluster together")
print("   • king/queen closer to each other")
print("   • cat/dog closer to each other")
```

sections.title: Real-World Example: Larger Corpus
sections.body:
```python
# Larger, more realistic corpus
realistic_corpus = [
    "machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence",
    "deep learning uses neural networks with multiple layers",
    "natural language processing deals with text and speech",
    "computer vision enables machines to interpret images",
    "neural networks are inspired by biological neurons",
    "the cat sat on the soft mat",
    "the dog played with a ball in the park",
    "cats and dogs are popular pets",
    "the king ruled the kingdom with wisdom",
    "the queen was loved by her people",
    "paris is the capital of france",
    "london is a major city in england",
    "python is a popular programming language",
    "java and python are used for development",
    "algorithms are fundamental to computer science",
] * 200  # Replicate for better embeddings

# Tokenize
tokenized_corpus = [sent.split() for sent in realistic_corpus]

# Train model
model_large = Word2Vec(
    sentences=tokenized_corpus,
    vector_size=100,
    window=5,
    min_count=2,
    workers=4,
    sg=1,
    epochs=100
)

print("✅ Larger model trained!")
print(f"   Vocabulary size: {len(model_large.wv)}")
print(f"   Embedding dimension: {model_large.wv.vector_size}")
```

```python
# Explore similarities
test_words = ['python', 'king', 'cat', 'learning']

for word in test_words:
    if word in model_large.wv:
        print(f"\n🔍 Most similar to '{word}':")
        similar = model_large.wv.most_similar(word, topn=5)
        for sim_word, score in similar:
            print(f"   {sim_word:15s}: {score:.4f}")
```

sections.title: Comparing CBOW vs Skip-gram
sections.body:
```python
import time

# Train CBOW
start = time.time()
model_cbow = Word2Vec(
    sentences=tokenized_corpus,
    vector_size=100,
    window=5,
    min_count=2,
    sg=0,  # CBOW
    epochs=50
)
cbow_time = time.time() - start

# Train Skip-gram
start = time.time()
model_skipgram = Word2Vec(
    sentences=tokenized_corpus,
    vector_size=100,
    window=5,
    min_count=2,
    sg=1,  # Skip-gram
    epochs=50
)
skipgram_time = time.time() - start

print("⚡ Training Speed Comparison:")
print(f"   CBOW:      {cbow_time:.2f} seconds")
print(f"   Skip-gram: {skipgram_time:.2f} seconds")
print(f"   CBOW is {skipgram_time/cbow_time:.1f}x faster!")
```

```python
# Compare quality on a test word
test_word = 'python'

if test_word in model_cbow.wv and test_word in model_skipgram.wv:
    print(f"\n📊 Similar words to '{test_word}':")
    print()
    print("CBOW:")
    for word, score in model_cbow.wv.most_similar(test_word, topn=5):
        print(f"   {word:15s}: {score:.4f}")
    
    print("\nSkip-gram:")
    for word, score in model_skipgram.wv.most_similar(test_word, topn=5):
        print(f"   {word:15s}: {score:.4f}")
```

sections.body:


sections.title: Key Parameters Explained
sections.body:
```python
Word2Vec(
    sentences=corpus,
    vector_size=100,      # Embedding dimension (50-300 typical)
    window=5,             # Context window (5-10 typical)
    min_count=5,          # Ignore rare words (frequency < 5)
    sg=1,                 # 0=CBOW, 1=Skip-gram
    epochs=5,             # Training iterations
    negative=5,           # Negative sampling (5-20)
    ns_exponent=0.75,     # Negative sampling distribution
    alpha=0.025,          # Learning rate
    min_alpha=0.0001,     # Minimum learning rate
    workers=4             # Parallel threads
)
```

### Tuning Guidelines

**vector_size**:
```
• Small corpus: 50-100
• Medium corpus: 100-200
• Large corpus: 200-300
• More dimensions → Better quality but slower
```

**window**:
```
• Small window (2-3): Captures syntactic relations
• Large window (5-10): Captures semantic relations
• Larger → More context but noisier
```

**min_count**:
```
• Keep rare words: min_count=1
• Typical: min_count=5
• Large corpus: min_count=10+
```

sections.title: Summary: Word2Vec
sections.body:
### Key Advantages
```
✓ Dense, low-dimensional vectors
✓ Captures semantic similarity
✓ Word analogies work!
✓ Fast training (even on CPU)
✓ Works well with moderate data
```

### Limitations
```
✗ One vector per word (no context)
✗ Can't handle OOV words
✗ No subword information
✗ Needs large corpus for quality
```

### When to Use
```
✓ Have moderate-to-large corpus
✓ Need semantic similarity
✓ Downstream task (classification, clustering)
✓ Don't need contextualized embeddings
```

### Next Steps
```
→ Use pre-trained Word2Vec (Google News)
→ Try GloVe (global context)
→ Try FastText (handles OOV with subwords)
→ For context: Use BERT/transformers
```
